**2026-11-19.** **Templates gain an `xmlEscape` helper,** so free text relayed into an XML message
stays well-formed. **Timers no longer fall behind under sustained load:** the engine fired at most
about 64 timers a second, whatever the shard count, so at higher rates every parked timer fired
later than the one before it. **A distribution's version line may carry its build** without the
build leaking into image tags. There is no migration, and no archive format, deploymentId or
snapshot format change.

## Before you upgrade

**Check these against what you run:**

- **Deployments that expect timer surges should run more than one shard** (`sutra.engine.shards`,
  `SUTRA_ENGINE_SHARDS`; default `1`). Due timers are now fired as fast as they fall due instead of
  32 per deployment per half-second tick. With one shard, that timer work shares the single
  execution lane with new work, so new-instance latency rises while a timer backlog drains: in the
  test below, at 200 new instances a second each parking a 1 s timer, the new-instance answer p50
  went from 2.5 ms to 59 ms at one shard, and from 1.9 ms to 2.6 ms at four.

## `xmlEscape`

`{{xmlEscape value}}` renders the string form of `value` with `&` `<` `>` `"` `'` replaced by
`&amp;` `&lt;` `&gt;` `&quot;` `&apos;`, for element content and attribute values alike. A null or
missing value renders empty; every other character, non-Latin scripts included, passes through
unchanged. Default `{{x}}` interpolation is unchanged and still renders verbatim, so escaping is
opted into per value. The template analyzer treats `xmlEscape` as a helper, so its argument is
reported as the model reference.

## Timers

- **What was wrong.** Once per 500 ms tick the timer poller claimed at most 32 due timers per
  deployment, fired them, and waited for the next tick: about 64 timer fires a second for the whole
  cluster (the poller runs on the leader only). Above that rate the backlog grew without bound.
  Releases up to 0.6.24 are affected. New-instance work never took this
  path, so its latency stayed flat while timer-driven follow-ups ran minutes late.
- **What changed.** Each tick keeps claiming while a claim comes back full, round-robin over the
  deployments still behind, until every claim comes back short, a drain budget of one second (or
  the tick, if longer) is spent, or the replica loses leadership. Each round's fires finish before
  the next claim. Up to `max(shards, 16)` timers fire at once, up from the shard count. Timer start
  events are unchanged. No new configuration key, and delivery stays at-least-once.
- **Measured** (debug build, PostgreSQL 16, each instance parks a `PT1S` timer then sends a
  follow-up; lag is the follow-up's arrival against its due time):

| Shards | Rate × 15 s | Follow-up lag p99, before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 200/s | 31.8 s | 0.78 s |
| 4 | 400/s | 78.2 s | 0.50 s |

  The remaining lag is the poller's 500 ms tick.

## Distributions

- **`sutra_cli::product_version()` reads the version up to the first ` (`.** A distribution whose
  version block starts `2.0.0-rc.6 (1a2b3c4, built 2026-11-16)` reports `2.0.0-rc.6` as its
  version, so the runtime image tag, the release tag `create app` scaffolds and `codecs` no longer
  carry the build suffix. A version block with the build on its own line works as before.

## Image scan

Six advisories published 2026-11-17 against the distroless base have no Debian fix and are
time-boxed to 2026-12-16 in `.trivyignore.yaml`. Three are glibc iconv converter over-reads
(CVE-2026-121757, CVE-2026-121758, CVE-2026-124024): the engine imports no iconv function. Three
are libssl3 issues (CVE-2026-107493, CVE-2026-124709, CVE-2026-35190): the engine does not load
libssl3 (its only dynamic libraries are libgcc_s, libm, libc and the loader), and the Kafka
client's compiled-in OpenSSL 3.6.3 is a TLS client over TCP that calls none of the affected
functions and runs no QUIC.
